name: memfd-then-execveat
why: memfd_create followed by execveat in the SAME pid within 10s is the fileless-execution correlation. The atomic open()s the payload first (fd 3), so the memfd is fd 4 (memfd_create exit=4, execveat a0=4). auditd logs execveat at syscall exit, AFTER the image is replaced, so that record carries the NEW image's comm 'memfd:atomic' and exe '/memfd:atomic (deleted)', not the pre-exec deteng_ values
source: recorded: strace+live run of memfd_exec_behavioral.c on this host -- memfd_create("atomic",0)=4, execveat(4,"",...,AT_EMPTY_PATH), post-exec comm=memfd:atomic exe=/memfd:atomic (deleted). (On older kernels the comm is the fd number, e.g. '6', as the benign slice has for runc.)

name: memfd-then-execveat-window-edge
why: the same pair 9s apart stays inside the 10s window; the correlation must still fire at the window edge. This dropper creates the memfd as its first fd (fd 3, a1=MFD_CLOEXEC), then fexecve's it; the execveat record carries the post-exec image (comm 'memfd:payload', exe '/memfd:payload (deleted)')
source: synthetic: a slower dropper, memfd_create and execveat 9s apart in one pid

name: memfd-create-only
why: a process that creates an anonymous memfd but never execs it (common for shared-memory buffers) is half the correlation; the execveat base must be required
source: synthetic: memfd_create used as a sealed shared-memory buffer, no exec

name: execveat-only
why: execveat of a real on-disk fd (fexecve of an O_PATH descriptor) with no preceding memfd_create is the other half; the memfd_create base must be required
source: synthetic: a launcher using fexecve on a normal file descriptor

name: memfd-and-execveat-different-pid
why: memfd_create in a parent and execveat in a forked child split the two syscalls across pids: the documented fork-variant coverage gap, which the pid group-by must enforce (mirrors controls/memfd_fexecve_in_child.c)
source: synthetic: memfd_create in pid X, fexecve in forked child pid Y, within 10s

name: memfd-then-execveat-too-late
why: the same pid does memfd_create and execveat but 20s apart, outside the 10s window; the timespan must bound the correlation
source: synthetic: memfd_create and execveat in one pid, 20s apart

name: runc-1.1-init-memfd-reexec-filtered
why: runc < 1.2 re-executes itself from a memfd on every container start and exec: runc init (comm exe, exe the runc binary) calls memfd_create, then execveat(fd, "", AT_EMPTY_PATH) in the same pid about 40 ms later. The runc_init filter on the memfd_create base suppresses it (the old rule fired on every container start)
source: runc v1.1.12 libcontainer/factory_linux.go (InitPath /proc/self/exe) and libcontainer/nsenter/cloned_binary.c (memfd_create("runc_cloned:/proc/self/exe"), fexecve); events as in the benign corpus docker run/exec templates

name: runc-path-memfd-wrong-comm
why: a memfd_create from a binary at a runc path whose comm is not runc init's `exe` (a binary dropped at /usr/bin/runc inside a container, which the kernel logs relative to the container's root) still fires: the runc_init filter needs both the comm and the path. The same binary run through a symlink or /proc/self/exe takes comm `exe` and is suppressed; see ldpreload-into-runc-as-exe-known-miss
source: synthetic: memfd_create then execveat in one pid, comm runc, exe /usr/bin/runc

name: ldpreload-into-runc-as-exe-known-miss
why: KNOWN MISS (a fileless execution that the runc_init filter suppresses): an unprivileged user runs the world-executable, dynamically linked /usr/bin/runc through a symlink named `exe` with LD_PRELOAD. The injected constructor's memfd_create carries comm `exe` and exe /usr/bin/runc, so the runc_init filter alone suppresses the correlation, and its execveat of the payload memfd follows in the same pid. It differs from runc init only in values the event schema does not carry (uid 65534 here, root for runc init) and in the memfd name. Labelled filtered because that is what the rule does with it today; if the filter is tightened (for example with a uid condition once the schema carries uid), this case fires and becomes a positive
source: recorded: on this host as uid 65534 (setpriv), `ln -s /usr/bin/runc lnk/exe; LD_PRELOAD=inj3.so lnk/exe --version`, whose constructor calls memfd_create("payload", MFD_CLOEXEC) and fexecve: printed pre-exec comm=exe exe=/usr/bin/runc memfd=3, post-exec comm=memfd:payload exe=/memfd:payload (deleted), same pid; strace: memfd_create("payload", MFD_CLOEXEC) = 3, execveat(3, "", ..., AT_EMPTY_PATH) = 0. uid and auid are kept from the audit record for a future uid-aware filter
